hook.text: Citrus greening disease has destroyed billions of dollars of Florida's orange groves. There is no cure.

buildup.text: Bacterial plant diseases enter through wounds, stomata, or insect vectors. Once inside, they're hard to stop.

discovery.text: Citrus greening bacteria live inside the plant's phloem—the nutrient highway. They block sugar transport.

twist.text: Tiny psyllid insects spread the bacteria from tree to tree. Controlling the vector is the only defense.

climax.text: Florida's citrus production has dropped 75% since greening arrived. The industry may not recover.

punchline.text: A microscopic bug carries a microscopic bacterium. Together they collapsed an industry.

quiz.question: How much has Florida's citrus production dropped since citrus greening arrived?

details.summary: Bacterial plant diseases cause wilting, rotting, and cankers that devastate crops ranging from tomatoes and potatoes to citrus and rice. This topic covers how bacterial pathogens infect plants, major bacterial diseases, and why they are especially difficult to treat.
details.whyItMatters: Unlike fungal diseases, bacterial infections in plants cannot be cured with fungicides. Once established, bacterial pathogens can persist in soil and plant debris for years, making prevention and resistant varieties the primary management tools.
takeaways: Bacterial wilt, fire blight, and citrus canker are among the most devastating diseases
Bacteria enter plants through wounds, natural openings, and insect-transmitted injection
No curative treatments exist for most bacterial plant diseases once infection occurs

faq.question: How do bacterial diseases differ from fungal diseases in plants?
faq.answer: Bacterial diseases cannot be treated with fungicides and have no curative chemical options once established. Bacteria reproduce much faster than fungi, spread through water splash and insects, and can persist in soil for years. Management relies heavily on prevention and resistant varieties.

faq.question: What are the most economically important bacterial crop diseases?
faq.answer: Ralstonia solanacearum causes bacterial wilt in over 200 plant species including tomatoes and potatoes. Citrus greening (HLB) spread by psyllids has devastated Florida's citrus industry. Fire blight caused by Erwinia amylovora destroys apple and pear orchards worldwide.
